title: I took a night job watching an empty parking garage. Rule four says never count the cars.
story:
The guard office is a glass box on level one, and the manager left me a laminated sheet of rules. Rule one, lock the stairwell doors at midnight. Rule two, ignore the elevator if it opens on its own. Rule three, headlights are fine, voices are not.

Rule four said never count the cars.

I figured that was a joke, until my third night. The garage is supposed to be empty after ten. But on the camera wall, I noticed cars on level three that had not been there at ten. Just a few. Then more.

I started counting. I couldn't help it. Eleven cars. Then I blinked, and there were fourteen.

None of them had plates. All of them faced the exit ramp, engines off, windows fogged from the inside.

At 3 AM I counted again to be sure. Forty-one cars across the whole garage, and one empty space, directly under my camera.

I switched to the last rule on the sheet, written in pen, in handwriting that wasn't the manager's. Rule five, if the count ever reaches the number of spaces, the doors are no longer locked from the inside.

I looked at the screen.

Forty-one cars. Forty-two spaces.

Something parked behind my glass box.
premise: garage night shift rulebook; counting the cars gives a number that grows
